findings.reason: The protected solution is already a conventional optimal sweep: sort starts and ends separately, release every room whose meeting has ended, allocate for the next start, and retain peak occupancy. Its variables describe genuine sweep concepts and the implementation is concise and interview-quality, so no candidate is justified.

The app-local and immutable Accepted native sources have identical empty guard, event arrays, end cursor, release loop, room updates, peak update, and return behavior; only typing syntax and the required LeetCode class-method wrapper differ.

The legal 32/128/512-meeting tiers make every interval active at the peak and exercise the full event sweep. The current source passes at +0.01 relative exponent with a 1.00x largest runtime ratio; a correct implementation that recounts active intervals at every start passes every output and fails only scaling at +1.10 with a 106.05x ratio.

The Approach proves peak simultaneous occupancy is both necessary and sufficient, accurately states the two-array costs, labels touching endpoints and the single-meeting boundary, and no longer presents an empty schedule as part of the source contract.
The hash-bound Premium Reference remains verified against the source structure, preserving both factual examples, minimum-room semantics, and both constraints.

coverage: both source-fidelity-verified examples remain first as visible samples with their exact schedules and minimum room counts
the former empty schedule was removed because the verified source requires at least one interval; a singleton [0,1000000] now covers the legal minimum count and both time limits
an unsorted touching chain proves rooms are released before a meeting beginning at the same time is allocated
three-way overlap followed by a touching meeting, fully nested intervals, and equal starts exercise distinct ways the occupancy peak can arise
a staggered schedule combines end/start ties with a later three-room peak so the result cannot be inferred from any one endpoint group
all eight authored room counts matched an independent oracle that counts active half-open intervals at every meeting start
5,000 seeded random schedules matched after shuffling, confirming input-order independence
constructed 10,000-meeting probes covered both the minimum possible answer of one and the maximum possible answer of 10,000
the protected current source passed all eight correctness rows and all three unchanged benchmark tiers through the real-test engine; every benchmark output was correct and scaling passed
all eight correctness rows are visible samples or trials, while the unchanged 32, 128, and 512-meeting workloads remain hidden performance-only benchmarks
